title: Report completed events clearly
lessons:
## What you will do
Report what happened, put completed actions in order, ask about a recent experience, and explain a service problem. Listen for actions and outcomes rather than translating each word. The production tasks are original learning practice, not official TCF scoring tasks.

## Prerequisites and quick check
Recall present avoir: `j'ai, tu as, il a, nous avons, vous avez, ils ont`; and être: `je suis, tu es, elle est, nous sommes, vous êtes, elles sont`. These mean I have/you have… and I am/you are… . You also need negation and Chapter 9 agreement. Before starting, describe your current location and ask a colleague a question. If these forms are uncertain, practise the auxiliary aloud before adding another verb.

## 1. A completed action: two parts, one tense
The passé composé normally combines present avoir or être with a past participle. It can correspond to English I did, I have done, or sometimes I did do; do not translate English auxiliary words one by one. `J'ai envoyé le document.` — I sent/have sent the document. The auxiliary changes with the subject; the participle identifies the action. Regular -er verbs usually make -é: parler → parlé, travailler → travaillé. Regular second-group -ir verbs make -i: finir → fini, choisir → choisi. Many -re verbs make -u: vendre → vendu, attendre → attendu. These are useful patterns, not a rule for every verb with those infinitive endings.

Learn frequent irregulars as chunks: `j'ai eu` — I had; `j'ai été` — I was/have been; `j'ai fait` — I did/made; `j'ai pris` — I took; `j'ai mis` — I put; `j'ai dit` — I said; `j'ai écrit` — I wrote; `j'ai lu` — I read; `j'ai vu` — I saw; `j'ai reçu` — I received; `j'ai ouvert` — I opened; `j'ai pu` — I was able to; `j'ai voulu` — I wanted to; `j'ai dû` — I had to; `j'ai connu` — I knew/met; `j'ai appris` — I learned. Keep the circumflex in dû. `J'ai dû annuler.` — I had to cancel, with an infinitive after dû.

## 2. Choose the auxiliary by the verb's construction
Most verbs use avoir, including movement verbs such as marcher, courir and voyager: `Nous avons marché jusqu'au lac.` — We walked to the lake. A frequent group uses être: aller, venir, arriver, partir, entrer, sortir, monter, descendre, rentrer, retourner, rester, tomber, naître, mourir, and related verbs such as revenir. `Elle est arrivée tôt.` — She arrived early. With ordinary être verbs, agree the participle with the subject: `Ils sont partis.` — They left. `Elles sont venues.` — They came.

Several verbs change auxiliary when they take a direct object: `Elle est sortie.` — She went out. `Elle a sorti les poubelles.` — She took the bins out. `Nous sommes montés au troisième étage.` — We went up to the third floor. `Nous avons monté les valises.` — We carried the suitcases up. Do not use être for every physical movement or avoir for every action involving an object somewhere in the sentence. Look at the actual construction.

## 3. Agreement without guessing
With avoir, there is no agreement with the subject: `Elles ont acheté une table.` — They bought a table. Agreement normally occurs with a direct object placed before the participle: `La table qu'elles ont achetée est solide.` — The table they bought is sturdy. For now, recognize this pattern and produce it in short familiar phrases. An indirect object introduced by à does not trigger that agreement: `Je leur ai téléphoné.` — I called them.

Pronominal verbs use être: put the reflexive pronoun before the auxiliary: `Je me suis levé.` — I got up, said by a male speaker; `Je me suis levée.` — the same, said by a female speaker. In familiar self-directed actions with no later direct object, the participle often agrees with the subject: `Elles se sont préparées.` — They got ready. But agreement depends on object function, not just être: `Elle s'est lavé les mains.` — She washed her hands. Les mains is the following direct object, so lavé does not agree with elle. `Elles se sont parlé.` — They spoke to each other. Parler à makes se indirect, so no agreement. `Les mains qu'elle s'est lavées…` — The hands she washed… has a preceding direct object and agreement. Learn these contrasts; do not add -e automatically after every reflexive verb.

## 4. Questions, negatives and sequence
`Avez-vous reçu mon message ?` — Did you receive my message? `Est-ce que vous êtes arrivé ?` — Did you arrive? In ordinary speech, rising intonation also works: `Vous avez réservé ?` — Did you book? Put ne…pas around the auxiliary: `Je n'ai pas compris.` — I did not understand. With reflexives: `Elle ne s'est pas inscrite.` — She did not register. Common adverbs often fall between auxiliary and participle: `J'ai déjà payé.` — I have already paid. `Nous n'avons jamais essayé.` — We have never tried. Use d'abord, ensuite, puis, enfin for first, next, then, finally. `D'abord, j'ai appelé. Ensuite, j'ai rempli le formulaire.` — First I called. Then I filled in the form.

English-speaker traps: say `J'ai visité Montréal.` — I visited Montreal, not a present form plus an English-style -ed equivalent. Say `Je suis allé au bureau.` — I went to the office, not j'ai allé. Do not choose passé composé simply because an English sentence has was; background and habits will need the imparfait in Chapter 11.

## 5. Hear the tense
In `j'ai parlé`, ai and the final -é are separate vowel signals; the written r of parler is absent from parlé. In `elle est arrivée`, hear the link between est and arrivée. Written agreement is often inaudible: arrivé, arrivée, arrivés and arrivées commonly sound alike. Do not rely on audio alone for spelling. Compare `il a pris` — he took, and `il est parti` — he left, as complete chunks. Synthetic voice practice supports decoding, not authentic-exam equivalence. Failed audio is a reason to retry, not record a listening success.

## 6. Try first
A. Report that two women arrived and took a taxi. B. Negate I have already paid using not yet. C. Complete the wash contrast for a woman: she washed herself / she washed her hands. D. Explain two completed actions after missing a delivery.

:::answer
A. `Elles sont arrivées et elles ont pris un taxi.` — They arrived and took a taxi. B. `Je n'ai pas encore payé.` — I have not paid yet. C. `Elle s'est lavée. Elle s'est lavé les mains.` — She washed herself. She washed her hands. D. Example: `J'ai appelé le livreur, puis j'ai choisi une autre date.` — I called the delivery driver, then chose another date. Other coherent actions are valid.
:::

## 7. Integrate, retrieve, revisit
Do the audio tasks before revealing scripts. Read for who did what and what remains unresolved. In speaking, report a fresh event with a beginning, two actions and an outcome; do not recite the model. In writing, check auxiliary choice separately from participle spelling. Reuse Chapter 9 to compare the service before recommending a solution. Divide bank 001–100 into four sets of 25; vary listening, retrieval and production rather than translating everything. For a four-hour session, allow 35 minutes recall, 45 listening, 40 reading, 45 speaking, 45 writing and 30 correction. Revisit errors tomorrow, in three days, a week and two weeks. Log whether the problem is auxiliary, participle, agreement or message clarity; write one corrected example and retell the event without notes. Objective answers and self-assessment measure different things; neither is an official NCLC result.

activities.title: A delivery account
activities.prompt: What happened after the customer called the shop? Listen before revealing.
activities.script: Le livreur est venu mardi, mais il a apporté une table au lieu d'une étagère. J'ai refusé le colis et j'ai appelé le magasin. Une employée a vérifié ma commande, puis elle a proposé une nouvelle livraison gratuite. J'ai accepté vendredi matin. Je n'ai pas demandé de remboursement.
options: The customer accepted a free replacement delivery.
The customer paid an extra delivery fee.
activities.explanation: After checking the order, the employee offered a free new delivery, which the customer accepted for Friday. No refund or extra fee was requested.

activities.title: After a community event
activities.prompt: What did the volunteers do before leaving?
activities.script: Notre atelier de réparation a attiré vingt personnes. Nous avons réparé des lampes et deux petits vélos. Une participante a apporté du café pour tout le monde. À la fin, nous avons rangé les outils, nettoyé les tables et noté les objets à réparer la prochaine fois. Ensuite, nous sommes partis ensemble.
options: They tidied up and recorded unfinished repairs.
activities.explanation: The closing sequence includes putting tools away, cleaning tables and noting objects for next time. Coffee was brought by a participant, not purchased by the volunteers.

activities.title: A repair record
activities.passage: Intervention du 12 novembre : le technicien est arrivé à neuf heures. Il a remplacé le joint du robinet et vérifié l'écoulement. La fuite a cessé. Il a aussi examiné le radiateur, mais il n'a pas pu le réparer sans une pièce spéciale. Le bureau a commandé cette pièce. Un second rendez-vous reste à fixer.
activities.explanation: The tap leak stopped. The radiator repair requires an ordered part and a second appointment that has not yet been scheduled.

activities.title: A registration problem
activities.passage: Bonjour, je me suis inscrite à l'atelier photo samedi. J'ai payé par carte et j'ai reçu un reçu, mais aucune confirmation de place. J'ai vérifié mon dossier : mon adresse électronique est correcte. Pouvez-vous me confirmer mon inscription avant que je réserve mon transport ? Merci, Nadia.
options: To confirm her place before booking transport.
activities.explanation: Payment and a receipt exist, but Nadia lacks confirmation of a place. She requests that confirmation before making transport arrangements.

activities.title: Report an unexpected incident
activities.prompt: Invent a recent minor incident at a class, shop or station. Tell a staff member what happened, what you did, what someone else did, and what you need now. After 60 seconds, add a detail in response to the imagined question: Did anyone help you? Do not read the model.
activities.model: Bonjour, je suis venu chercher mon sac à la consigne. J'ai tapé le code, mais la porte n'a pas bougé. J'ai essayé une deuxième fois, puis j'ai demandé de l'aide à une agente. Elle a vérifié mon reçu et elle a appelé le responsable. Personne n'a encore ouvert le casier. Oui, l'agente m'a aidé, mais elle n'a pas trouvé de solution. Pouvez-vous ouvrir le casier ? Mon train part bientôt.
rubric: Fulfillment: states incident, actions, help and present request.
Range: uses multiple action verbs and sequencing phrases.
Control: auxiliary choice, participles and negation are mostly reliable.
Intelligibility/register: polite, audible and responsive rather than recited.

activities.title: Explain a failed service
activities.prompt: Write 90–130 words to a service provider. Invent a missed or incorrect service, give the sequence of events, mention evidence you kept and request a concrete remedy. Learning task; no official score conversion.
activities.model:
Bonjour,
J'ai réservé un nettoyage pour mardi matin. Votre employé est arrivé à dix heures et il a vérifié les pièces. Ensuite, il a reçu un appel et il est parti sans terminer le travail. J'ai appelé votre bureau, mais personne n'a répondu. J'ai donc pris des photos des pièces et gardé le reçu du paiement. Je n'ai pas encore reçu d'explication. Pouvez-vous proposer une nouvelle intervention gratuite cette semaine ? Je suis disponible jeudi après-midi. Merci de confirmer l'heure et le nom de la personne avant son arrivée. Je peux vous envoyer les photos si nécessaire.
Cordialement,
Amine
rubric: Fulfillment: gives events, evidence and a specific requested remedy.
Range: uses action vocabulary and a clear request.
Control: checks avoir/être, irregular participles and negation.
Register: factual, polite service email; stays within the learning word range.
